lesson.title: Review: Putting a Full Paragraph Together
lesson.subject: ela

contentBlocks.text: All week you've built one piece at a time: topic sentence, supporting details, transitions, concluding sentence. Today, combine everything into one real, finished paragraph.

Quick review: a strong paragraph has a topic sentence (Day 1), 2-3 specific supporting details (Day 2) connected with transition words (Day 3), and a concluding sentence that restates the main idea in new words (Day 4). Gather everything you wrote this week and combine it into one clean, complete paragraph — read it aloud to check that it flows smoothly from start to finish.
You just wrote a complete, well-structured paragraph using all four pieces you learned this week. This same four-part structure will support every paragraph you write from now on.

objectives: Recall all four components of a strong paragraph: topic sentence, supporting details, transitions, concluding sentence
Combine the week's separate pieces into one complete, well-organized paragraph
teacherGuide.facilitationScript:
1. Do the quick walk-through review of all 4 days together, out loud.
2. Have the child gather and combine all 4 pieces into one finished paragraph on the worksheet.
3. Read the finished paragraph aloud together, checking flow and that the concluding sentence isn't a verbatim copy of the topic sentence.
4. Celebrate finishing a real, complete piece of writing — the whole week built toward this one finished paragraph.
5. Note this same 4-part structure (topic sentence/details/transitions/conclusion) will apply to every future paragraph-writing unit.
differentiationTips: Struggling: allow light editing help (spelling, minor wording) as long as the 4-part structure is the child's own work
Ready for more: ask them to add one more supporting detail beyond the 3 they already have, adjusting transitions as needed
This is a genuine finished-writing milestone — treat it as something worth celebrating, not just another worksheet
teacherGuide.answerKey: Answers will vary — check the finished paragraph includes all 4 required parts (topic sentence, 2-3 connected supporting details, concluding sentence) and reads as one coherent paragraph, not four disconnected sentences.
teacherGuide.standardsRationale: Synthesizes the full week's Common Core Grade 4 Writing standards (W.4.2a-e) into one complete piece of student writing, matching the course's own 'multi-paragraph essays' description as the foundational single-paragraph skill it builds from.
